Angle to lead with: The 3 a.m. question and what came of it; first print copy photo
What this round should teach you: Whether the story reads to people who know you.
Result: 850 views / 367 viewers. 31 reactions (23 like, 6 love, 2 wow). 12 comments. 1 share. 5 link clicks. 0 new follows. 779 of 850 views were existing followers.
Top objection raised: None. Twelve comments, all warm. The AI provenance went completely unchallenged.
Change it triggered: Treat Stage 1 as an affection test, not a reception test. Do not read it as validation of the framing. Also: put the site link in the post body next time.
Notes: Copy saved in docs/launch-copy/facebook-2026-09.md. Two signals worth carrying: one commenter read it as 'I didn't know you are a Buddhist', so the personal frame can eclipse the book; and the Gen-Z question drew zero answers, so it is not the engagement hook you hoped.

What this round should teach you: Does honest AI provenance read as credibility or as a red flag to professional contacts? This is the answer that matters for AI training work.
Result: PROVISIONAL, still climbing. 47 impressions at 3h, 70 at 4h. 3 reactions, 2 real comments. Engagement rate about 7 percent, which is healthy for LinkedIn. Baseline for this account over the prior 3 weeks: 1,525 / 634 / 330 / 263 / 191 / 140, median around 296. Update once matured at 24-48h.

Change it triggered: Earlier read of 'no reach' was premature: the post was just slow to start, and the engagement rate is now good enough to keep distribution expanding. The one durable lesson is not to edit after publishing.
Notes: Draft in docs/launch-copy/linkedin-draft.md. Lead with method, not conversion. Link in first comment; LinkedIn throttles body links.
